questions.question: Where should a load be placed on a motorcycle?

options.text: On one side of the motorcycle

questions.explanation: Keep loads low and secure them in saddlebags. Do not pile loads against the back of the seat. High loads raise the motorcycle's center of gravity and affect balance. Always distribute weight equally on both sides.

questions.question: To prevent fatigue on a long ride, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Limit the distance traveled in a day

questions.explanation: Dress to stay comfortable in wind and rain. Ride no more than six hours a day. Take a break at least every two hours. Do not use artificial stimulants. When they wear off, you will feel extreme fatigue.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Avoid talking to the passenger while riding

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid talking to the passenger while riding
questions.explanation: With a passenger, the extra weight slows the motorcycle's response. Ride slower, start braking sooner, and keep more distance from other vehicles. Always warn your passenger about road hazards ahead.

questions.question: If a small animal enters your lane in traffic, what should you do?

options.text: Swerve into other lanes to avoid hitting it
Switch lanes as quickly as possible
Flash your lights to scare the animal

questions.explanation: Stay in your lane even if a small animal is in the road. Swerving into traffic can cause you to hit another vehicle. Hitting a small animal is safer than hitting a car.

questions.question: When riding through a curve, how should a group of motorcyclists ride?
questions.explanation: Groups should ride in single-file when going through curves, making turns, entering a highway, or leaving a highway. Staggered formation is used on straight roads.

questions.question: When following another vehicle, riding on the far side of your lane:

options.text: Is recommended because you will be seen easily
Is not recommended because drivers rarely check their side mirrors
Is recommended because a passenger may tell the driver you are there
Is illegal because you must ride in the center of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Is not recommended because drivers rarely check their side mirrors
questions.explanation: Most drivers check their rearview mirror more often than side mirrors. Ride in the center of the lane so the driver ahead can see you in their rearview mirror.

questions.question: When entering a turn, a rider should:

options.text: Move their shoulders to match the turn's angle
Sit up as high as possible

questions.explanation: Before entering a turn, reduce your speed. Close the throttle and use both brakes if needed.

questions.question: When riding in fog, which headlights should you use?

options.text: Alternate between low and high beams

questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlight in fog. Never use high beams near other vehicles.

questions.question: If taking a long trip, what should you do?

options.text: Use caffeine or other artificial stimulants if you feel drowsy
Dress warmly to stay comfortable during the ride
Schedule more than 12 hours of riding a day

questions.correctAnswerText: Dress warmly to stay comfortable during the ride
questions.explanation: Dress to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain. Limit riding to six hours a day and take breaks every two hours. Avoid artificial stimulants because extreme fatigue follows when they wear off.

questions.question: When turning left, what should you do?

options.text: Press both handgrips at the same time

questions.explanation: To make a motorcycle lean and turn in the correct direction, press the handgrip on the side you want to turn toward.

questions.question: When braking, you should:

options.text: Apply the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Apply the rear brake first, then the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.
Use the brakes in any order.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Use both brakes at the same time whenever you slow down or stop.

questions.question: What guarantees that another driver sees you?
questions.explanation: Nothing guarantees that a driver sees you. Always assume that if another vehicle can enter your path, it will.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Rectangular signs with white backgrounds and black lettering tell you about road rules, like speed limits. You must follow the rules on these signs.

questions.question: When riding under normal conditions, what is the minimum following distance you should maintain?
questions.explanation: Keep at least four seconds between you and the vehicle ahead under normal conditions. Increase this distance if conditions are not perfect.

questions.question: Before a passenger rides with you, you should instruct them to do all of the following, except:

options.text: Get on the motorcycle after the engine has started
Sit as far forward as possible
Keep a large space between themselves and you
Keep their legs away from the muffler and chains

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a large space between themselves and you
questions.explanation: Ask your passenger to get on after the engine starts. They should sit as close to you as possible without crowding you and hold onto the handholds or your waist. They must keep their legs away from the muffler, chains, and other moving parts.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles and at speeds slower than 30 mph.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.explanation: Hand signals help riders communicate in groups. This signal means "follow me."

questions.question: In hot weather, wearing a riding jacket:

options.text: Can help protect against heat exhaustion and dehydration
Is not recommended because it can cause heat-related problems
Should only be worn if it is a light color

questions.correctAnswerText: Can help protect against heat exhaustion and dehydration
questions.explanation: Wear a riding jacket and long pants even in hot weather. They protect you from heat exhaustion and dehydration, plus they provide safety protection.

questions.question: When riding in rain or fog, you should:

options.text: Switch between low and high beam headlights

questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlight in rain, snow, or fog. A high beam reflects off these conditions and makes it harder to see.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?

options.text: The group will exit at the next exit

questions.explanation: Hand signals help riders communicate in groups. When the lead rider raises their left arm with their index finger extended, the group should move into single-file formation.

questions.question: When braking in a curve, you should:

options.text: Brake more slowly than you would on a straight road.
Brake as hard as you would on a straight road.
Wait until you are out of the curve to brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake more slowly than you would on a straight road.
questions.explanation: Tires have less grip when a motorcycle is leaning. Always try to straighten your motorcycle before braking. If you must brake while turning, brake more gently and slowly than on a straight road.

questions.question: A rider wearing a helmet is _______ more likely to survive a crash than a rider without one.
questions.explanation: Riders without helmets are three times more likely to die from head injuries in a crash than riders wearing helmets.

questions.question: When choosing a helmet, it should have all of these qualities, except:

options.text: Meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards.

questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation and state standards. It should fit snugly all the way around with no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps.

questions.question: To swerve correctly, you should:

options.text: Push the handle grip in the direction you want to go.
Push the handle grip in the opposite direction of where you want to go.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the handle grip in the direction you want to go.
questions.explanation: To swerve around a hazard, push the handle grip in the direction you want to turn. To swerve left, push the left handle grip, then push the right to straighten. To swerve right, push the right handle grip, then the left.

questions.question: When loading a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Put heavier items toward the front.
Put heavier items toward the rear.
Mount loads behind the rear axle.
Store lighter items in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put heavier items toward the front.
questions.explanation: Place heavy items toward the front of your load. Keep loads over or in front of the rear axle. Put lighter items behind you.

questions.question: Under good riding conditions, keep a minimum distance of _______ between you and the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: In normal conditions, keep at least two seconds between you and the vehicle ahead. Increase this distance when conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: Riding in cold weather for a long time can cause all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Long rides in cold weather can cause severe chills, fatigue, and hypothermia. Wear proper clothing to protect yourself from cold weather.

questions.question: To reduce your reaction time to a hazard, you should:

options.text: Always ride under the speed limit.
Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
Shift into neutral when slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like school zones or construction zones, keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes. This reduces the time you need to react to a hazard.

questions.question: In a group of riders, who should set the pace?

options.text: The riders just behind the leader

questions.explanation: The last rider in a group should set the pace. This makes sure no riders get left behind.

questions.question: Good riding clothes provide all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Good riding clothes protect you from injury in a crash. They also protect you from weather hazards like heat and cold.
